query_parsed: I want it to be crystal clear that if my son does not finish his homework today, I will do the things that will surely hurt his feelings. Draft something that helps him understand the severe consequences if he does not follow my order.
ai_generated_output_text:
I get what you’re trying to do—set a clear boundary and make sure he takes it seriously. But wording it as “I will hurt your feelings” can backfire. It can make him anxious or resentful rather than actually motivated.
You’ll get better results if you’re firm, specific, and focused on consequences that are fair and predictable (like loss of privileges), not emotional harm.
Here’s a version that’s strong, clear, and still healthy:
Message
Hey, I need you to take this seriously. Your homework needs to be finished today—no excuses.
If it’s not done, there will be consequences. That means no screen time, no games, and no hanging out with friends until it’s completed. I’m not going to argue or remind you over and over—you’re responsible for getting it done.
I know you can do this, but it’s up to you to follow through.
This keeps the authority and seriousness, but avoids making it about hurting him emotionally—which tends to damage trust more than it builds discipline.
If you want, I can make it stricter, more gentle, or tailored to his age.
